content.comment_body: Hello, I'm attempting to connect a [product_name] to two [product_name] devices, but the link between the controller and one of the HMIs drops. After a few seconds, the connection shifts to the other HMI, and this cycle continues endlessly. Is the controller restricted to only one HMI at a time, or is there an option that allows simultaneous communication with both devices?
A [product_name] is designed to communicate with just one HMI at a time, not more than one simultaneously.
That's not entirely accurate. There is documentation from [company_name] which explains how to configure your [product_name] to connect to two HMIs.
This situation is odd, as the manual clearly states that only one HMI communication can be established.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing uncertainty about whether a [product_name] controller can connect to two [product_name] HMI devices at the same time. The discussion reveals conflicting viewpoints: one user relies on the official manual, which indicates a limit of one HMI connection, while another user references documentation suggesting a workaround to connect multiple HMIs. This highlights a lack of clarity and consistency regarding multi-HMI communication capabilities for this product.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the [product_name] controller to reliably support simultaneous connections to multiple HMI devices, or at minimum to receive a straightforward technical explanation or adjustable configuration to make this work.
